You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the monoclinic space group Pc (No. 7, Hall symbol P -2yc), with all atoms occupying general 2a positions related by the symmetry operation (x, y, z) and its glide-equivalent partner. The input unit cell contains 20 atoms with composition Sr₂Nd₂Ni₂Ru₂O₁₂, corresponding to two formula units of SrNdNiRuO₆. The lattice parameters of the input cell are a = 5.536862 Å, b = 5.473125 Å, c = 9.74746341 Å, with α = 55.80234639°, β = 90.0°, and γ = 90.0°. This is a nonstandard monoclinic setting; the transformation from the input fractional coordinates to the standard frame is given by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the matrix P has rows (−2.1555186031528183×10⁻¹⁷, 1.0, 1.9999999999999998), (−1.0, 5.0062488163961066×10⁻¹⁷, 0.0), and (−1.0777593015764092×10⁻¹⁷, 3.2965924989117753×10⁻¹⁸, 0.9999999999999999), and the origin shift s is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). All fractional coordinates below are given in the input frame and were rounded to six decimal places.

The ten crystallographically independent orbits, each of multiplicity 2, are distributed as follows. Strontium occupies the 2a site at (0.743274, 0.218902, 0.749404), while neodymium sits at (0.265927, 0.298716, 0.251797). The two transition-metal sites are nickel at (0.501383, 0.242546, 0.000805) and ruthenium at (0.002359, 0.245881, 0.499703); these two sites are separated by approximately half a lattice vector along c, consistent with an alternating arrangement of Ni and Ru layers perpendicular to the long axis.

Six independent oxygen orbits complete the structure. The first oxygen site lies at (0.659555, 0.043917, 0.453518), the second at (0.318177, 0.471340, 0.540132), the third at (0.247404, 0.045190, 0.045566), the fourth at (0.736062, 0.471598, 0.958558), the fifth at (0.847066, 0.237922, 0.257682), and the sixth at (0.178795, 0.271095, 0.742836). Each of these oxygen positions, like the cation sites, generates a second atom through the c-glide plane perpendicular to b, yielding the full complement of twelve oxygen atoms per unit cell.

No positional corrections beyond the six-digit rounding were required; the listed coordinates represent the input geometry directly. The arrangement places the larger Sr and Nd cations in distinct layers along the c direction, with the smaller Ni and Ru cations occupying separate sites between them, and the oxygen sublattice distributed among six general positions that bridge the metal layers in three dimensions.
